It was winter, and on

A-cup of coffee was what

B-that cold day a hot

C-I needed desperately
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **BAC.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

The part which comes first in the sequence should suitably follow the preposition *on.* Part B seems to be appropriate. ‘It was winter, and on that cold day…’ seems logically correct.

The next in sequence is the one that follows the adjective *hot*. So, part A seems correct to be second in the sequence followed by part C.

*It was winter, and on that cold day a hot cup of coffee was what I needed desperately*

Thus, the sequence is BAC, making **option 4** the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

He had had a short illness, there (had been) a brief time of acute suffering, then all was over.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is : (4) **No Improvement**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us consider a sentence: I have had a meeting with the president.
 
• This sentence is in the present perfect tense__ as it talks about a past action that is continuing into the present.
 
• Here, In this sentence, there are two verbs have and had. 
 
• The first** have** is auxiliary also known as the* helping verb* and the second **had** is the* main action verb.*
 
• A sentence may or may not have an auxiliary verb but it’ll "always" have a main or verb.
 
• Now, when we use the same sentence in past tense it changes to: __ I had had a meeting with the president__. 
 
• The main verb here is ***had*** that’s why we are ending up with "double *had'*.
 
• Some more examples will help us to understand this by changing the tenses from present to past:
 
 
• I have had a busy week - I had had a busy week
 
• She have had some troubles - She had had some troubles
 
 
 
• Now, the first part of the sentence is in the past perfect (had + verb).
 
• Here, the verb is also *had*. (That’s why double had).
 
• The rest of the sentence should also be in the past perfect tense (been is the verb).

Thus, no improvement is required. **Option 4** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

She said to me, “I like your smartphone .”

options.text: She told me that she liked my smartphone.
She said that she like my smartphone.
My smartphone was liked by her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **She told me that she liked my smartphone**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Direct speech__, the message is conveyed in the words of the author or concerned person.
 
• In __Indirect speech__, the message is conveyed in our words. 
 
• When we convert Direct speech to Indirect speech, we omit the inverted commas.
 
• The conjunction that is added before introducing the words spoken between quotation marks (“…”).
 
• We also use conjunction that before reporting the statement within “ - ” marks in our own words.
 
• The tense of the reported speech in the indirect speech depends upon the tense of the reporting verb in the direct speech. If the reporting verb is in the past tense, the verb in the reported speech undergoes a backshift in tense. Here, 'like' will change into 'liked'.

Thus, applying these fundamental rules, the sentence in the Indirect speech is: *She told me that she liked my smartphone.*

*​**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 Eats

questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the usual speed of the train be ‘x’ km/hr.

Time taken to cover 200 km = Distance/Speed = 200/x hrs.

But, when the train left 1 hour left,

Speed of train = (x + 10) km/hr.

⇒ Time taken = Distance/Speed = 200/(x + 10)

⇒ (200/x) - 1 = 200/(x + 10)

⇒ (200 - x)/x = 200/(x + 10)

⇒ (200 - x)(x + 10) = 200x

⇒ 200x + 2000 - x² - 10x = 200x

⇒ x² + 10x - 2000 = 0

⇒ x² + 50x - 40x - 2000 = 0

⇒ x(x + 50) - 40(x + 50) = 0

⇒ (x - 40)(x + 50) = 0

⇒ x = 40, - 50

∵ Speed cannot be negative,

∴ **Usual speed of train = 40 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Let the usual speed of the train be x km/hr.

⇒ 2000 = x(x + 10)

⇒ 40 × 50 = x × (x + 10)

⇒ 40 × (40 + 10) = x × (x + 10)

x = 40 km/hr

**∴ Usual speed of train = 40 km/hr.**

• The uneven heating of the regions of the troposphere by the sun causes convection currents, and large-scale patterns of winds that move heat and moisture around the globe.

questions.question: A Sonar of a ship sends sound waves of speed 1500 m/s. These waves are reflected back by the ocean floor in 5 seconds. Find the depth (in m) of the ocean floor.
questions.solution:
Given:-

Speed of sound waves = 1500m/s

Total time (time to go + time to come back) of waves = 5sec (2.5 each)

Thus, depth (distance) of the ocean floor = speed × time

= 1500 × 2.5 = 3750m

questions.question: Living things constitute the biotic component of the ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Biosphere.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• The biosphere is the global ecological system integrating all living beings and their relationships, including their interaction with the elements of the lithosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere.
 
• **Living things constitute the biotic component of the biosphere**.
 
• The lithosphere consists of the earth's crust and upper part of its mantle.
 
• The atmosphere is what we call 'the air,' or the mixture of gases held around the earth by its gravitational pull.
 
• The hydrosphere is the total sum of all of earth's water in any form, whether it's on the ground as liquid or ice, or in the clouds as water vapour.
 
• The biosphere is the fourth sphere and consists of the places where life can be found. Since life exists in the air, on and in the earth, and on and in water, the biosphere overlaps, connects, and influences all the other spheres - and they all affect the biosphere.
 
• **The mesosphere** and thermosphere are the layers of the atmosphere of the Earth.
 
• **The heliosphere **is a bubble-like region in space which is dominated by the Sun and extends far beyond the orbit of Pluto.
